I see his face—clear as day—when I’m driving, even when I’m just stopping at a light. It just *pops* in, outta nowhere. Sometimes my hands start shaking on the wheel.

I’m always on edge, like something bad’s about to happen, even when it’s not. I jump at noises, get angry fast—last month I threw a coffee cup so hard it broke the mirror in my cab. I know it’s too much, but I can’t hold it back. My ex-wife said I became cold, distant. Even when I got that big safety bonus last quarter, I didn’t feel anything. No pride, no joy—just hollow. 

And the anxiety? It’s not just general worry. It *starts* when I pass that stretch of highway, or when I hear sirens. It’s like I’m back there. I avoid certain routes now, not just because of traffic—but because of *that* road. It’s all tied to that one night.

I’ve been married for five years, and I used to find such peace in my work—spending hours restoring old paintings, the quiet, the precision. But since the accident—when my car was hit head-on during a snowstorm last year—I can’t seem to come back to myself. Just hearing tires skid on wet pavement makes my chest tighten and my hands shake like I’m right back in that moment. The fear doesn’t fade; it’s like I’m still trapped in the split second the glass shattered.  

I love my husband, I do, but I can’t feel it the way I used to. I see him looking at me, waiting, and I want to reach out, but I’m just… empty. I broke one of his mother’s vases the other day—out of nowhere, I snapped—just because he asked if I wanted to talk about it. I didn’t mean to, but the words felt like an accusation, and I threw it.  

I stay on edge all the time. And yes, I’m anxious—but only about things tied to that day, like storms or driving. It’s not general; it’s like my body remembers the crash before my mind does. Everything I avoid, everything that sets me off… it all goes back to that moment.
